title: Operator acceptance protocol for identity & keying workflows
creator: Aanya Kapoor
description:
Purpose: Define a lightweight, testable operator acceptance protocol that teams can use to verify SSO/SAML integrations, RBAC role mappings, audit log completeness, and KMS/HSM key lifecycle behaviors for Private (VPC/on-prem) customer onboarding. This ticket owns the PRD that clarifies ambiguous requirements discovered during the last two pilot onboards and produces a single sign-off checklist + deterministic acceptance test matrix for Operator teams and Security reviewers.

Scope (in):
- SSO / SAML: assertion validation, attribute mappings, assertion replay protection, upstream IdP metadata ingest and verification, SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows.
- RBAC: role hierarchy, default deny policies, cross-tenant resource scoping, automation for role grants during onboarding, and admin emergency access paths.
- Audit logging: immutable event stream for authn/authz events, key access & rotation events, operator actions, and tenant-specific audit export. Log schema, retention guidance, and evidence export for audits.
- KMS/HSM: customer key import/export policies, operator key escrow patterns, rotation procedures, HSM-backed signing for binary artifacts, and failure-mode behavior (operator access removal, emergency recovery).
- Acceptance artifacts: conformance checklist, automated end-to-end test scenarios, sample audit export package, and operator runbook.

Out of scope:
- Full legal contract wording for key escrow (deliver separate legal ticket).
- Re-architecting storage for audit retention longer than 7 years.

Requirements summary:
1) Security: All operator actions that modify key material or RBAC grants must produce signed audit events with non-repudiable markers; logs must include requestor identity, correlation_id, timestamp, and pre/post state hashes.
2) SSO/SAML: The system must accept IdP metadata in XML and OIDC discovery, validate certificates (CRL/OCSP optional but documented), and support SAML assertion encryption and signed responses.
3) RBAC: Support canonical roles: tenant-admin, tenant-operator, read-only-audit, service-account; allow custom role definition but require approval for any role that grants key export.
4) KMS/HSM: Support both provider-managed KMS and customer-provided HSM (PKCS#11 interface). Key rotation must be able to be automated or manual with an operator-confirmation step; rotation events produce audit evidence.
5) Evidence & Tests: Provide a downloadable audit evidence package (logs + verification script) and 10 deterministic E2E tests that Security can run in staging.

Acceptance criteria and sign-off are enumerated below. The PRD includes explicit SLOs for operator response times during onboarding and defined rollback paths in case a keying operation fails.

Intended reviewers: Security Eng, Platform Eng, Customer Ops, Legal (for escrow notes).
acceptance_criteria: All operator-modifying key and RBAC actions emit signed audit events with required fields (requestor, correlation_id, timestamp, pre_state_hash, post_state_hash)
SAML uploads accept and validate IdP metadata and certificates; test IdP integration passes SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows in staging
RBAC role model implements canonical roles and enforces default-deny; attempts to create 'key-export' roles require explicit approval UI flow
KMS integration supports both provider KMS and PKCS#11 HSM in staging; key import and rotation flows complete without errors and produce audit evidence
Automated E2E test suite of 10 scenarios passes in the Private staging environment and is runnable by Security within a single shell script
Operator runbook exists with step-by-step recovery actions for failed rotations and emergency key revocation; runbook reviewed and approved by Customer Ops
Evidence export bundle (logs + verification tool) demonstrates chain of custody for a sample key rotation within 15 minutes
Security sign-off obtained and recorded in the checklist with timestamp and reviewer name
